_about: The houses are hostile to each other (VAMILY row [houses at war]). WHO is at war with whom is NOT stored here: it is read from bohemia_between.js (the canon graph's own edges, war flag and sign). This file holds only Battle Brothers' rules for what a war DOES, each quoted, and our mapping of them, each marked ours. Measured before building: the between table already exists and parties are already SENT at their hostiles; what never happened is two parties of different factions MEETING, and on the real valley they do, a few times a day (6 seeds, 4 waking days: 4 to 16 war meetings, 2 to 13 hostile ones).

war_takes_settlements.quote: The Noble Houses declare war on each other. They begin to take over rival settlements reducing those settlements supply/wealth levels without destroying them.
war_takes_settlements.reading: a base the world takes in a war is Conquered, not burned

side_makes_enemy_hostile.quote: taking one side makes the enemy side hostile which, while opening up opportunity to kill and pillage, locks you out of a significant portion of the map.
side_makes_enemy_hostile.why: the wiki says hostile; the Hostile band's top (9) is the bar that makes hostility, read from relations.json by name, never lower than it already is

holy_war.quote: Noble houses hostile to southern City States during the Holy War
holy_war.note: a second war kind; not built here, named so it is not forgotten

meeting.why: a meeting is two parties of different factions within one cell; counted once a day per pair so a standoff is one event, not hundreds

war.why: strength is the act power column the parties module already carries; no new number

hostile_not_war.why: the graph says prey-tax and not war ('war would be expensive, and this pays'): a tax is an event, a party is not destroyed
